item.title: Iranians fleeing cities under attack seek refuge in the countryside
item.summary: Tens of thousands of Iranians are fleeing Tehran and other cities as Israeli and U.S. bombardment spreads fear

item.title: US allies and rivals in Asia gauge fallout from war in the Middle East
item.summary: North Korea, South Korea, Japan, and China are watching warily as war spreads across the Middle East

item.title: As pope seeks dialogue and diplomacy, 2 US cardinals reject US-Israeli war in Iran
item.summary: Pope Leo XIV is calling for an end to the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran and expressing deep sorrow for those killed

item.title: Russia and Ukraine both claim front-line progress with US-brokered talks on hold
item.summary: Russian and Ukrainian officials are making contradictory claims of battlefield successes in their 4-year-old war

item.title: UN peacekeepers defy South Sudan military's order to leave opposition-held town
item.summary: The United Nations Mission in South Sudan says it will not comply with a government order to shut down its base in Akobo, an opposition stronghold near the Ethiopian border where tens of thousands of refugees have fled

item.title: Human Rights Watch details deaths and injuries of police drone attacks in Haiti
item.summary: Human Rights Watch says drones operated by Haitian security forces and private contractors have killed at least 1,243 people and injured 738 others

item.title: A 1-pound lawsuit puts Gerry Adams’ alleged IRA role on trial in London
item.summary: Former Sinn Féin leader Gerry Adams faces a civil lawsuit in London that accuses him of being an Irish Republican Army leader responsible for bombings in England

item.title: Several dead after postal bus bursts into flames, authorities say
item.summary: Police say several people are dead and several others were injured after a postal bus caught fire in a town west of the Swiss capital

item.title: China announces resumption of passenger trains to North Korea after COVID
item.summary: China has reopened passenger train service to North Korea, ending a long COVID-era shutdown and boosting cross-border travel

item.title: Hungary orders authorities to hold some $82 million in seized Ukrainian cash and gold
item.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has ordered that a shipment of Ukrainian cash and gold seized last week by Hungarian authorities be held in custody for up to 60 days while his country’s tax authority investigates the case
